reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) and 4 (anchored) — the spec's own declared-rect rule, violated by six of its items
gaps.problem: §4 states 'Measurement rects are declared, not eyeballed... The critic measures those rects and no others', then six items measure regions that probes.json has no key for: item 3's 'an isolated lamp head' halo profile, item 9's '32 px band along a building base or kerb' and 'more than 200 px from any junction', item 10's 'alpha-cut foliage pixels', item 11's 'anything at ≥ 0.6 × focus' (a depth-based selection the spec itself declares ungradable in item 12: 'a depth-reconstructed normal is not gradable — declare the rect instead'), item 12's '≥ 250 distinguishable streaks' (no counting method given), and item 22's 'a high-contrast edge in the same shot (a lane marking)'. These are the module's headline items — AO, bloom, DOF, sharpen. The critic will pick one band and the builder another, and each disagreement costs a round to re-shoot at 30–390 s per frame.
gaps.fix: Extend the probes.json schema in §4 with the keys these items need and require them in the same deliverable: `lampHead: [x,y]` (a point; the halo profile is measured radially from it), `aoJunctionBand: [x,y,w,h]` (the 32 px band), `aoOpenGround: [x,y,w,h]` (the >200 px-from-any-junction control), `foliageRect: [x,y,w,h]`, `sharpenEdge: [x0,y0,x1,y1]` (the lane-marking segment, profiled perpendicular), and for item 11 `nearObject`/`farObject` rects on the photo shot in place of the '≥ 0.6 × focus' depth selection. For item 12, name the counting method explicitly: connected components of the `_override({rain:0})` diff thresholded at 8 luma, components of 12–2000 px accepted, count ≥ 250.

gaps.property: 1 (sequenced) and 3 (numeric) — the round-2 cut line leaves five of twenty-four items unclassified
gaps.problem: The cut line says round 2 must pass items 1–9 and 14–19, and that 12–13 and 20–21 may slip to round 3. Items 10, 11, 22, 23 and 24 appear in neither list. Item 24 (degrades without environment) is a whole extra probe URL and two shots; item 11 (DOF off) demands an override A/B on all sixteen standard shots plus four presets. A builder rationing SwiftShader capture time has to guess whether those are this round's work or next round's, and the critic has no stated basis for failing the round if they are missing.
gaps.fix: Assign every item. Suggested: fold 10, 11 and 24 into the must-pass set (10 and 11 are free riders on the AO and DOF A/B passes already required by 9 and the DOF-off decision; 24 is two cheap shots), and add 22 and 23 to the deferrable set alongside 12–13 and 20–21 with the same 'list as deferred with a one-line reason in docs/builds/effects_r2.json' rule. State the count explicitly: 'must-pass: 1–11, 14–19, 24 (18 items). Deferrable: 12, 13, 20, 21, 22, 23.'

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) — the shot matrix contradicts itself, and the shot item 13 is graded on is in no list
gaps.problem: §4 defines the standard set as sixteen shots plus 'the declared presets plaza, lamps, glare, photo at 12 and 22' — eight preset shots. Item 14 then grades 'all 16 standard shots, all four preset shots'. Four or eight is not a rounding difference: it decides whether glare_12/glare_22/photo_12/photo_22 must be error-free. Worse, item 13 requires the glare preset at --time 17.5, and glare_17p5 appears neither in §4's matrix nor in §8's 'Also required in the round's shot set' list — so a builder who shoots exactly what §8 enumerates fails item 13 by construction, and a critic who shoots exactly §4's matrix cannot grade it.
gaps.fix: Fix §4 to read 'plus the declared presets plaza, lamps, glare, photo at 12 and 22 (8 shots) and glare at 17.5 (1 shot) = 25 shots', change item 14's 'all four preset shots' to 'all nine preset shots', and add `--camera glare --time 17.5` to §8's explicit shot list next to the rain and 720p calls.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — item 2 can fail on pixels effects does not own, and it fights item 1
gaps.problem: Item 2 measures mean(R) − mean(B) ≥ 25 over every pixel ≥ 200 luma at 22:00 in skyline_22 and street_22. The ≥200 population is not restricted to the ground: environment's stars (src/modules/environment/sky.js:114-128, ~1.3 px at 1080p, drawn white-blue and scaled by uStarBright) and the moon disc land in it, and item 1 simultaneously requires ≥ 0.20 % of pixels ≥ 200 in skyline_22 while item 2's second clause requires the sky to stay blue. Star brightness belongs to environment; effects' only lever is a global grade, which would break items 1, 5 and 8. This is an acceptance item that can fail for a reason outside the blast radius, with no core-request escape valve named (unlike the fog in-scatter, which the spec handles correctly).
gaps.fix: Scope item 2's emissive population the way item 3 already scopes bloom: 'among pixels ≥ 200 luma that lie inside the dilated emitter mask (§4 convention)', or 'among pixels ≥ 200 luma below the declared skyline rect'. Add the same escape valve as the golden-hour failure mode: if the sky itself makes the item unreachable, file it in docs/core-requests/effects.md against environment's uStarBright and ship the frame that passes under the masked measurement.

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) — the acceptance list's capture cost is never costed, and no cheaper resolution is authorised
gaps.problem: The A/B items imply roughly thirty extra 1080p renders on top of the 25-shot matrix: item 11 alone needs a dof-on/off pair on all sixteen standard shots plus four presets, items 3, 4, 9, 10, 13 and 18 add more, and each override pair is two frames. §6 records that round 1 lost 12 of 16 gauntlet shots to timeouts on this box and that a 1080p frame costs 30–390 s. The spec tells the builder to 'budget the captures' and to shoot the must-pass matrix first, but never does the arithmetic and never authorises a cheaper capture size for diffs — even though item 19 establishes that the 1280×720 frame tracks 1080p within |Δp50| ≤ 4.
gaps.fix: Add one line to §4's conventions: 'All _override / setEnabled / setDebugView A/B diffs are captured at 1280×720 unless the item says otherwise; per-item pixel-percentage thresholds are resolution-independent and the px distances in items 3, 12 and 13 scale by 0.667 at 720p (halo 13–47 px, streaks 8–27 px long, glare 53–173 px).' Then state the expected total capture count so the builder can plan: '25 matrix shots at 1080p + ~30 A/B frames at 720p.'

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — five numbers with no named observation method
gaps.problem: Item 16's 'JS heap grows < 2 MB over 300 frames' and 'update() costs ≤ 0.5 ms' name no probe and no resolution; at 1080p under SwiftShader 300 frames is 30–75 minutes, so the number as written is unmeasurable in this environment — precisely the case property 3 says must be flagged and substituted, and the spec flags it correctly for elapsedMs but not here. Item 17's 'adaptation reaches within 1 % of its steady value in ≤ 4 rendered frames' has no stated observation either, and screenshot.mjs hardcodes headless=1 (tools/screenshot.mjs:22), which is exactly the branch where the spec says adaptation is instantaneous — so the non-headless behaviour is never captured by any tool in the repo. The §5 budget table's two texture-memory rows put an arithmetic breakdown in the 'How it is checked' column instead of a check; renderer.info.memory.textures is a count, not bytes.
gaps.fix: Name the probes. Item 16: 'measured in shots/effects/r<n>/apicheck.mjs at 640×360 with speed=1, sampling performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize and __sim.stats().moduleMs.effects every 50 frames over 300 frames; report both series in the build record.' Item 17: 'the same probe reads state().grade.blackPoint on frames 1–8 with headless=0 in the URL.' §5: add `state().vram = {chainMB, sceneMB}`, computed in-module as the sum of w·h·bytesPerPixel over owned render targets and of texture dimensions over staged materials, and grade the two memory rows against that field.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — item 18's 'flat' bypass tolerance is unmeasurable as written
gaps.problem: Item 18 requires setPreset('flat') to differ from setEnabled(false) by '≤ 0.5 % of pixels by > 2, AA aside'. 0.5 % of 1920×1080 is 10 368 pixels; a dense city frame with the stage item 20 demands has far more than 10 368 geometry-edge pixels, and SMAA is still in the chain under 'flat' (the spec lists only grade, bloom, AO, glare and rain as off). 'AA aside' has no operational meaning — the critic cannot separate an AA difference from a grade difference in the delivered PNG, so this clause is decided by whoever argues harder.
gaps.fix: Make the comparison AA-free: either 'setPreset("flat") also disables SMAA/FXAA, so the diff against setEnabled(false) is measured with no exclusion' or 'the diff is measured after a 3×3 box blur of both frames, and pixels within 2 px of a Sobel edge (threshold 30 luma) in the setEnabled(false) frame are excluded'. Either resolves it; the first is cheaper.

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) and 5 (bounded blast radius) — two undeclared derived budgets and an unstated asset route
gaps.problem: Item 15 caps the chain at 28 draw calls and the whole staged frame at 64, which leaves the stage exactly 36 calls — but the spec never states that, and §8/item 20 grow the stage from round 1's measured 19 calls to ≥6 towers, ≥10 mid-rise, ≥12 low-rise, roof clutter on ≥60 % of roofs, ≥4 facade families, 3 tree species with ≥3 clustered cards each, lamps, signage, a neon panel, terrain, a forest belt and a 2–4 km ridge. Separately, item 20 and §8 require ≥4 distinguishable facade material families naming brick and plaster, but the nine manifest sets §7 lists (asphalt_02, aerial_grass_rock, brown_mud_leaves_01, rock_face, aerial_beach_01, concrete_wall_008, concrete_floor_worn_001, gravel_floor_02, leafy_grass) contain neither. §7 says rain streaks, droplets and glare kernels must be procedural but is silent on facades, so the builder must guess between appending CC0 downloads to manifest.json and generating facades procedurally.
gaps.fix: Add to §5: 'Stage draw calls ≤ 36 (64 total − 28 chain); if the chain lands under 28 the surplus is not transferable — declare budget.drawCalls = 64 and report the split.' Add to §7 after the manifest list: 'brick and plaster are not in the manifest; generate them procedurally from assets.procedural.noiseTexture/gradient over concrete_wall_008 as a detail layer, or append CC0 entries and run tools/fetch-assets.mjs — state which route you took in the build record.'

strengths: Every code citation is verifiable and exact: effects/index.js:223 (_override), main.js:41/78/88-99 (the modules= degradation path), registry.js (apis[name] = def.api, no .api wrapper), constants.js:39-44 (QUALITY), world.js:84-88 (weather defaults), environment/index.js:104-107 and :272-281 (the nine extra published fields), gauntlet.mjs:23 vs screenshot.mjs:17 (the two different timeouts), screenshot.mjs:27 (t0 before browser launch). I checked all twelve; none drift.

World-data section is honest about paraphrase risk: it marks the first three lines as verbatim from ARCHITECTURE §3, flags the nine environment-published fields as NOT yet in §3, and schedules its own deletion via a core request once §3 absorbs them. That is the correct handling of a spec that would otherwise become a shadow authority.

Known failure modes are the real ranked issues from docs/critic/effects_r1.md (cream field at 17:30 with the bloom-diff-is-zero diagnosis, the 0.006/0.010/0.022 night lift, the fixed black point stacked on S-contrast stacked on an AO power term, uShadowTint.b, the leaf-halo AO, the 42 m DOF blob, the depth/readBuffer swap guard), each with the shot filename that shows it.

Correctly resolves a genuine ARCHITECTURE ambiguity: §4 says 'only environment and effects may' change renderer state, BUILDER.md says only environment sets toneMapping/exposure/fog. The spec names BUILDER.md as tie-breaker and confines effects to its own passes reading world.weather.exposure.

Catches a real defect in a role file (BUILDER.md's `ctx.modules.props?.api?.place?.()` — ctx.modules IS registry.apis, so the extra ?.api silently returns undefined) and routes the correction through docs/core-requests/ instead of editing BUILDER.md, respecting blast radius.

Budget is consistent with ARCHITECTURE §9 (28 ≤ 30 chain draw calls, 0.5 ms ≤ 2 ms module JS) and every tightening is stated with its reason; the elapsedMs-vs-initMs note is exactly the measurement-substitution property 3 asks for, backed by round 1's own 113 941–393 148 ms numbers.

Explicitly refuses to restate BUILDER.md's invariants (blast-radius discipline, fail-soft, determinism, honest self-scoring) and carries only the effects-specific twist on each — the separation the standard's role-prompt rule demands.

§4's measurement conventions (luma formula on the delivered 8-bit PNG, pN definition, sun-side half, the dilated setDebugView('mask') as the emitter definition, probes.json rects with a rejection rule for mislabelled rects) remove most of the usual builder/critic argument surface — where they are actually applied.

The round-2 cut line with an explicit trade ('a round that passes items 1–9 and defers the stage scores higher than a round that touches all 24 and lands none') plus capture ordering is real sequencing guidance under a known-scarce resource.
verdict:
8.0 — FAIL by 0.5. This is the most rigorously grounded module spec in the repo: I spot-checked twelve code citations (effects/index.js:223, main.js:41/78/88-99, registry.js apis, constants.js:39-44, world.js:84-88, environment/index.js:104-107 and :272-281, gauntlet.mjs:23, screenshot.mjs:17 and :27, debug.js __sim.registry) and every one is exact; the manifest name list matches public/assets/manifest.json verbatim; the dependency signatures (engine.setComposer/onResize/stats, camera.registerPreset/flyTo/screenToGround, assets.pbr/applyPbr/procedural, rng.*) all exist as written; the budget (chain ≤28 vs ARCHITECTURE §9's 30, update ≤0.5 ms vs §9's 2 ms) is consistent and the tightening is stated; the failure modes are the actual ranked issues from docs/critic/effects_r1.md, not generic advice; the round count is checked against STATUS.json (maxRounds 4, effects.next round 2) and corrected in the first paragraph; the elapsedMs-vs-initMs trap is exactly the kind of measurement-substitution property 3 demands; it correctly resolves ARCHITECTURE §4's renderer-state ambiguity against BUILDER.md; and it catches a real bug in BUILDER.md (`?.api?.` — ctx.modules IS this.apis) while correctly routing the fix through a core request instead of editing the role file. Properties 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 are handled by explicit, correct delegation to BUILDER.md rather than duplication.

What keeps it under 8.5 is not vagueness but self-inconsistency, and each instance costs a round. The spec establishes an excellent rule in §4 — "measurement rects are declared, not eyeballed", with the critic explicitly forbidden from measuring anything else — and then breaks it in items 3 (the "isolated lamp head"), 9 (the "32 px band along a building base or kerb" and "more than 200 px from any junction"), 10 ("alpha-cut foliage pixels"), 11 ("anything at ≥ 0.6 × focus", selected by a depth the spec itself says is not gradable in item 12), and 22 ("a high-contrast edge... a lane marking"). Those are five future arguments between builder and critic on the module's headline items. The round-2 cut line lists 1–9 and 14–19 as must-pass and 12–13, 20–21 as deferrable, leaving items 10, 11, 22, 23 and 24 unclassified — a builder under a 30–390 s-per-frame capture budget has to guess whether the degradation probe is required this round. §4 declares eight preset shots (plaza/lamps/glare/photo at 12 and 22) while item 14 grades "all four preset shots", and item 13 requires glare at 17.5, which appears in neither §4's matrix nor §8's shot list — so a builder who shoots §8's list fails item 13 by construction. Item 2 measures colour over every pixel ≥200 luma including the sky, where the stars and moon belong to environment and effects has no lever but a global grade. Three budget rows and two acceptance clauses (texture memory, the 300-frame heap walk, the ≤4-frame adaptation) name a number with no observation method in an environment where 300 frames at 1080p is 30–75 minutes. And the ~30 override A/B pairs the acceptance list implies are never costed, nor is a cheaper capture resolution authorised even though item 19 already proves 720p tracks 1080p within |Δp50| ≤ 4.

Fix the eight ranked gaps below — most are one or two lines each — and this is a 9.
